name: CIFAR-10
description: CIFAR-10 is a widely used benchmark dataset of 60,000 32×32 color images across 10 object classes, split into 50,000 training and 10,000 test images; it is used in this paper to study and benchmark ultra-fast training methods and augmentation strategies. The paper also references experiments on CIFAR-100, SVHN, CINIC-10, and ImageNet for generalization analyses, but CIFAR-10 is the primary dataset used for method development and timing/accuracy targets.
license: MIT License (as cited for the CIFAR datasets in Krizhevsky et al., 2009, per the paper’s references).
citeAs: Alex Krizhevsky, Vinod Nair, and Geoffrey Hinton. CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (Canadian Institute for Advanced Research), 2009. URL: http://www.cs.toronto.edu/~kriz/cifar.html.

creator.name: Canadian Institute for Advanced Research (CIFAR); authors: Alex Krizhevsky, Vinod Nair, Geoffrey Hinton

rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataCollection: Images are curated 32×32 color images labeled into 10 classes (original CIFAR-10 specification); in this paper the authors download via torchvision and store as tensors, applying normalization and augmentations (random/alternating horizontal flip, 2-pixel reflection-padding translation; Cutout only in some variants).
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and accelerating supervised image classification training; evaluating training speed to reach fixed accuracy targets (94%, 95%, 96%); studying augmentation strategies (alternating flip), test-time augmentation, optimization tricks, training variance and calibration; facilitating large-scale experimental iterations and statistical comparisons.
rai:responsibleAIMetadata.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of low-resolution object images and does not contain personal or sensitive information per the original dataset intent; no PII handling is discussed in this paper.
